string.text: Gold-plated Zippo lighter
Unremarkable flash drive

A flash drive with a sturdy metal case and sliding cap, engraved “CR.” Its contents and how it ended up here are unclear, but it looks well made. It should be inspected. 
 
 %c[0, 252, 186, 23] • %c[0, 156, 122, 39] Valuable item. Approximate value: enormous.

A beautiful, likely collectible gold-plated Zippo lighter with an engraved finish. Even in such harsh conditions, people still value luxury. Items like this are used for quick trades or an immediate bribe when transferring money is a hassle. 
 
 %c[0, 252, 186, 23] • %c[0, 156, 122, 39] Valuable item. Approximate value: low.
Squad leader’s notes

A Soviet field map case, apparently filled with a squad leader’s notes. Paper remains a reliable way to store information: PDAs run out of power and can be hacked. Some commanders carry a paper case the old-fashioned way. It holds valuable details such as mission objectives, orders, routes, supply caches, shifted radio frequencies, unit coordinates and call signs. A trader will pay well for it, since information is key in faction conflicts. 
 
 %c[0, 252, 186, 23] • %c[0, 156, 122, 39] A trader may be interested in this item.
Hard drive

A hard drive in a shockproof sleeve and bag—an unusual find in the Zone. Its contents are often software-encrypted and may include research results or military intelligence. The safest choice is to sell it to a trader for good money and let the information become their problem. 
 
 %c[0, 252, 186, 23] • %c[0, 156, 122, 39] Valuable item. Approximate value: average.
Gravity analyzer module

A gravity analyzer with a USB cable for a laptop, Professor Hermann’s invention. Unlike Sakharov, who relies on calculations and direct observation, Hermann belongs to the new school and favors technology. This costly module analyzes gravity anomalies and distortions. Something inside stays still relative to the ground as it is turned; its internals are unknown, but it is worth a great deal. 
 
 %c[0, 252, 186, 23] • %c[0, 156, 122, 39] Valuable item. Approximate value: above average.
Boss’s wristwatch

A fine mechanical watch with a huge, luxurious face. It is not very water-resistant, but unlike cheap quartz watches it survives near gravity anomalies. Known colloquially as a gang boss’s “kettles,” it is often worn by crime bosses—or those who hunt them. A prized barter item: quality Swiss watchmaking worth about one-fifth of a gold bar, and extremely expensive. 
 
 %c[0, 252, 186, 23] • %c[0, 156, 122, 39] Valuable item. Approximate value: above average.
Field scientist prototype

A field prototype used by scientists, packed with switches and a telescoping antenna. Since the birth of the Darkness, the Zone’s survival rules have changed: new anomalies are everywhere, and no one knows how to interact with or defend against them. Whoever learns first gains answers and fortune. Large funds now support anomaly research, including outside scientific groups, so unreliable empirical devices like this have appeared throughout the Zone. 
 
 %c[0, 252, 186, 23] • %c[0, 156, 122, 39] Valuable item. Approximate value: decent.
Optical analyzer module

An optical analyzer with a USB laptop cable, another of Professor Hermann’s inventions. This expensive module mounts on a tripod and examines anomalies from a distance. Its highly sensitive sensors may even measure local psi distortions. It costs a fortune and is useless to an ordinary stalker. 
 
 %c[0, 252, 186, 23] • %c[0, 156, 122, 39] Valuable item. Approximate value: high.
Mobile laboratory case

A large, heavy, sturdy case packed with scientific equipment: flasks, a computer screen, sensors, buttons and switches. This costly instrument is built for field analysis of samples, avoiding dangerous trips to a laboratory. Its preset algorithms can analyze soil, liquids and even artifact fragments. A lucky find for an ordinary stalker, as it costs astronomical sums. 
 
 %c[0, 252, 186, 23] • %c[0, 156, 122, 39] Valuable item. Approximate value: very high.
Mysterious locked case

A strange, heavy, incredibly sturdy case engraved with an atom and the code “0013.” It seems to have no lid, though a faint seam runs along its edge. Its origin and opening mechanism are unknown. Rumor says anomalies cannot affect it: slime slides off, and gravity anomalies ignore it. I would not test these stories, though I doubt them. 
 
 %c[0, 252, 186, 23] • %c[0, 156, 122, 39] Valuable item. Approximate value: very high.
